speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: He has asked for an assessment of Singapore-United States (US) bilateral ties.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore and the US enjoy a substantive, multifaceted and a very long-standing partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The fundamentals of this mutually beneficial relationship have been nurtured across both Democratic and Republican Administrations over the past 60 years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore worked closely with the Administration of former President Joe Biden.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: During this time, our bilateral ties broadened, we institutionalised cooperation in areas including space, critical and emerging technologies and nuclear energy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For example, in 2023, we established the US-Singapore Critical and Emerging Technology Dialogue, which bolsters our collaboration in cutting-edge technology.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In December 2024, the US-Singapore 123 Agreement entered into force and in January this year, we signed a Memorandum of Understanding Concerning Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Together, these agreements and partnerships will deepen civil nuclear cooperation, it will enable us to better understand how advanced nuclear energy technologies can potentially support our clean energy needs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In 2024, we also commemorated the 20th anniversary of the US-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (USSFTA).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This was the US’ first FTA with an Asian country and, in fact, remains its only FTA with an ASEAN country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Today, the US is our top trading partner in services, our second largest trading partner in goods and our largest foreign investor.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US has invested more in Singapore than it has invested in India, China, Japan and Korea combined.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is why we have 6,000, in fact, more than 6,000 US firms based in Singapore, creating jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Meanwhile, Singapore is the third largest Asian investor in the US and there are some 200 Singapore companies in 40 states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Together, our bilateral trade and investments between the US and Singapore generate over 350,000 jobs in the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also worked well with President Donald Trump during his first term.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In October 2017, President Trump invited then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong to visit the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And of course, in June 2018, President Trump came to Singapore to attend the US-North Korea Summit.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In 2019, then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong and President Trump signed the Protocol of Amendment to the 1990 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Regarding the United States Use of Facilities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This extended the MOU by a further 15 years and it underscores our strong bilateral defence relationship and Singapore’s support for the US strategic presence in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We look forward to working closely again with President Trump to further deepen bilateral ties in the years ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US presence in our part of the world has actually helped to provide security, stability and economic opportunities in the Asia Pacific for the past 80 years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US is ASEAN’s second-largest trading partner and the largest source of FDI into ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has also supported ASEAN economic initiatives, especially capacity building in areas like digital trade, trade facilitation and the development of micro, small and medium enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US has also cooperated closely with ASEAN on emerging issues like clean energy and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the world is now at a new inflection point, probably at a point which we have not faced for almost a century.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The liberal world order that prevailed after the Second World War, which was characterised in three dimensions: one, domestically, usually democracy and human rights; two, economically, by global supply chains and economic integration; and three, at the international level by the development of international institutions, the United Nations, the Bretton Woods institutions, international law, international norms and rules.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That liberal world order, which, in fact, has been quite conducive for Singapore’s progress in the last 60 years, is now being eroded and it is being eroded because it has lost domestic political support in many parts of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I set that out so that we can also situate the changes which are happening within the US and the unfolding drama of its relations with its own treaty allies, with Europe, with China, with Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And therefore, how we need to respond to this profound challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US’ relationship with China is, in fact, the most consequential relationship in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: How these two superpowers interact with one another has deep implications for global stability and prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Right now, I would characterise it as a significant lack of strategic trust between these two superpowers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we are all witnessing a bifurcation, a decoupling of the global economy as a result of that.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But again, if you look at the headlines over the last few days, it is not just the US and China, but also its relationship within its own allies and neighbours in its own hemisphere, and its evolving relationship with the European Union (EU).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And the challenge, therefore, is how Singapore and Southeast Asia should respond.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We believe there needs to be an omni-directional engagement on our part with all the multiple poles of power that are emerging.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That means, engaging with the US, engaging with China, India, the EU, Africa and South America.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And you would notice our intensive diplomacy and economic engagement across the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The signing of FTAs like the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, which is ASEAN with China, Japan, Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: You would have noticed the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), which initially was supposed to include the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US pulled out, the rest continued and the TPP has grown since then.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is worth noting that all these FTAs that Singapore has been able to sign have occurred despite the mood against globalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And in fact, if you look at the variety of governments in charge of these countries, they range across a very wide political spectrum.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the point is we can still continue to engage and make common calls as widely as possible in order to expand opportunities and to look for stability.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Specifically, with respect to Singapore, we will have to continue to play a constructive, inclusive role in a nimble way given our size.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, that means, we have to be consistent, reliable and a trustworthy host to enterprises from all over the world, including the US and China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will uphold the rule of law and sanctity of contract.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will act decisively and firmly against individuals and companies that flout the rules.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Or maybe, let me rephrase that more colloquially.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It means playing it straight, it means saying the same thing to everyone and it means doing what we say.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At a time of tension, instability and volatility, our Singapore branding and the way we speak and behave, in fact, becomes more valuable.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I know we are under time pressure so, obviously, I cannot give the Member a comprehensive answer to all that and, in any case, the news is still unfolding.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, this is an area which we are watching very, very closely but I hope Members in this House will recognise that it still means we need to keep calm, we need to keep our eyes open.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we need to be very careful in what we say and how we behave and playing it straight, saying the same thing to everyone and meaning, and doing what we say, is valuable.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I do need to prepare Singaporeans that it will be a turbulent ride in the months or years to come.
